info.name: PaperBoy — Dynamic variables
info.description: Every Postman dynamic variable PaperBoy has an opinion about, one request per outcome. Import this and read CONVERSION-NOTES.md: the first two requests should generate no notes at all, the third should note two computed rows, and the last should list the values you must supply yourself.

item.name: Built in/A GUID and an ISO timestamp
item.description: $guid, $randomUUID and $isoTimestamp all have exact Hurl equivalents, so these become {{newUuid}} and {{newDate}} and the request needs nothing supplied to run.

item.name: Built in/The same GUID twice
item.description: One dynamic variable used in a header and in the body. Hurl's {{newUuid}} is evaluated per use, so these two are deliberately allowed to differ — the request is here to prove the import doesn't emit two rows for one name.

item.name: Computed/A Unix timestamp and a random integer
item.description: $timestamp is Unix seconds and $randomInt is 0-1000 inclusive. Neither is a Hurl built-in, so each arrives as a row in the [Gen] block. Used twice apiece to check exactly one row is written per name.

item.name: Supplied/Faker data nothing can produce
item.description: Postman's faker variables have no honest equivalent. These are renamed so the file still parses and listed in CONVERSION-NOTES.md as values to supply — inventing a name would send a plausible wrong value, which is harder to notice than a request that refuses to run.

item.name: Supplied/All three kinds in one request
item.description: The mixed case: a built-in, a computed row and a supplied value side by side, so the preview shows all three placeholder colours at once.
